citeAs: Gokaslan, A., Cooper, A. F., Collins, J., Seguin, L., Jacobson, A., Patel, M., Frankle, J., Stephenson, C., Kuleshov, V. (2023). CommonCanvas: An Open Diffusion Model Trained with Creative-Commons Images. arXiv:2310.16825.
creator: Aaron Gokaslan, A. Feder Cooper, Jasmine Collins, Landan Seguin, Austin Jacobson, Mihir Patel, Jonathan Frankle, Cory Stephenson, Volodymyr Kuleshov (Cornell Tech, Databricks Mosaic)
description: CommonCatalog-CC-BY (CommonCatalog-C) is a dataset of approximately 26 million Creative-Commons-licensed images sourced from YFCC100M that are licensed for commercial use, paired with high-quality synthetic captions generated using a pre-trained BLIP-2 model. It is a subset of the larger CommonCatalog-NC dataset and is used to train the CommonCanvas family of text-to-image diffusion models.
name: CommonCatalog-CC-BY
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Captions were synthetically generated using the pre-trained BLIP-2 OPT2.5B model (telephoning). The model was chosen based on qualitative analysis and its state-of-the-art performance on MS COCO. Images were center-cropped and resized to 512x512 before captioning. The process required approximately 1,120 GPU A100 hours.
rai:dataBiases: The YFCC100M data is about a decade old, so CC images are not as current as those in LAION-2B. Synthetic captions show reduced diversity of n-grams compared to ground-truth captions. The model underperforms in categories like faces, general photography, and paintings, which are categories from the Conceptual Captions dataset relying on web-scraped data. CLIP Score may favor SD2 since CLIP is trained on similar text style as LAION.
rai:dataCollection: Images were sourced from the YFCC100M dataset by re-scraping from Flickr using the IDs provided in the YFCC100M metadata. Only Creative-Commons-licensed images were retained, excluding those with non-derivative (ND) licenses. The resulting images are very high resolution (exceeding 4K). CommonCatalog-C contains only images licensed for commercial use (CC-BY and CC-BY-SA), while CommonCatalog-NC additionally includes non-commercial CC licenses.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Raw source data is the YFCC100M dataset, consisting of 100 million CC-licensed images and multimedia files from Flickr, with Flickr IDs linking to the original data. The images in the original YFCC100M dataset were low-resolution; the authors re-scraped them from Flickr to obtain high-resolution versions exceeding 4K.
rai:dataLimitations: CommonCatalog contains only roughly 70 million CC images, which is much smaller than LAION-2B's roughly 2 billion images. The YFCC100M data is about a decade old, so images are not as current as those in LAION-2B. Synthetic captions have reduced n-gram diversity. Although images are CC-licensed, adversarial prompts can still produce content resembling iconic characters.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Images were filtered by Creative-Commons license type, excluding non-derivative (ND) licenses. For caption generation, images were center-cropped and resized to a maximum size of 512x512 pixels before being passed to BLIP-2. At training time, all images remain in their native resolution.
rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset is designed to address copyright concerns in training generative models by using only openly-licensed Creative-Commons images with known provenance, as an alternative to web-scraped datasets like LAION-2B whose copyright status is legally uncertain. The dataset enables training of high-quality T2I models that are less likely to reproduce copyrighted characters or content.
rai:dataUseCases: Training text-to-image generative diffusion models, particularly as a copyright-safe alternative to web-scraped datasets. The commercial subset (CommonCatalog-C) is intended for training models for commercial use cases.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: BLIP-2 OPT2.5B (pre-trained image-to-text model) was used to generate synthetic captions for all CC images in CommonCatalog.

evidence.rai:dataCollection: We began with the YFCC100M dataset, which consists of 100 million CC-licensed images and multimedia files, as well as Flickr IDs linking to the original data. We therefore re-scraped these images from Flickr, based on the IDs provided in the YFCC100M metadata. Our scraped images are very high resolution (exceeding 4K), which makes them more suitable for T2I training.
evidence.rai:dataCollectionRawData: We began with the YFCC100M dataset, which consists of 100 million CC-licensed images and multimedia files, as well as Flickr IDs linking to the original data [59]. The images in the dataset associated with the original paper exhibit two issues that make it ill-suited for direct use to train Stable Diffusion: they are low-resolution, and many of them have licenses that do not expressly allow for the distribution of derivative works.
evidence.rai:dataCollectionType: We therefore re-scraped these images from Flickr, based on the IDs provided in the YFCC100M metadata. Our scraped images are very high resolution (exceeding 4K), which makes them more suitable for T2I training.
evidence.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: We exclude images with non-derivative (ND) licenses. To do so, we center-cropped and resized all of the images to a maximum size of 512x512 pixels. We perform these transformations because captioning images at native resolution would be very expensive. At training time of the diffusion model, all images remain in their native resolution.
evidence.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: We compared several captioning models and, based on qualitative analysis and its state-of-the-art performance on MS COCO, chose to use the pre-trained BLIP-2 OPT2.5B model for synthesizing CommonCatalog's captions. Based on these preliminary results, we captioned all of the YFCC100M Creative-Commons images, which required about 1,120 GPU A100 hours.
evidence.rai:machineAnnotationTools: We compared several captioning models and, based on qualitative analysis and its state-of-the-art performance on MS COCO, chose to use the pre-trained BLIP-2 OPT2.5B model for synthesizing CommonCatalog's captions [34]. BLIP-2 consists of three components: a pre-trained, frozen (i.e., fixed) visual encoder, a learned transformer network that converts the visual embeddings into a text prompt, and a frozen large language model (LLM) that takes in the prompt.
evidence.rai:dataBiases: An issue, which we do not address, is that the YFCC100M data is about a decade old; its CC images are not as current as those in LAION-2B. We also observed reduced diversity of n-grams in our synthetic captions, a pattern previously noted by Nguyen et al. [42]. It underperformed in several categories, including faces, general photography, and paintings.
evidence.rai:dataLimitations: An issue, which we do not address, is that the YFCC100M data is about a decade old; its CC images are not as current as those in LAION-2B. Although we train on Creative-Commons images, it is still possible for an adversarial prompt to produce content that, for example, includes iconic characters.
evidence.rai:dataSocialImpact: One could instead independently curate a dataset of CC-licensed images with known provenance that expressly allow for copying, adaptation, and commercial use. As constituent images can be stored and distributed, this would also solve the link rot problem, thereby enabling greater reproducibility. Qualitatively, our model deviated more from these characters than SD2.
evidence.rai:dataUseCases: We assemble a dataset of Creative-Commons-licensed (CC) images, which we use to train a set of open diffusion models that are qualitatively competitive with Stable Diffusion 2 (SD2). CommonCatalog-C only contains data from the bottom two (yellow) rows, reflecting images licensed for commercial contexts.
